title: Contractible incoming commas imply a left-anodyne monomorphism
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard horns, quasicategories, weak homotopy equivalences and weak contractibility of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and join slices of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Let $K,L$ be small quasicategories and $j:K\hookrightarrow L$ a degreewise injective simplicial map. For a vertex $l\in L$, define $L_{/l}$ in degree $a$ by maps $\Delta^a\star\Delta^0\to L$ with final vertex $l$, and let $K\times_L L_{/l}$ use the source projection $L_{/l}\to L$. Suppose every such comma quasicategory $K\times_L L_{/l}$ is weakly contractible, meaning its map to a point is a weak homotopy equivalence. Then $j$ is left anodyne: it belongs to the smallest class containing isomorphisms and all horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq1$ and $0\leq i<m$, and closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. The image of $j$ need not be a full simplicial subset of $L$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.3.1 (cofinality detected by comma categories), printed p.236, followed by Proposition 4.1.1.3(4) (a cofinal inclusion is right anodyne), printed pp.223-224, both applied to opposite simplicial sets. Independently read in the retained HTT.pdf text. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text:
Put $A=K^{\mathrm{op}}$, $B=L^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $i=j^{\mathrm{op}}$. Clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] says that opposites preserve quasicategories, while order reversal is a degreewise bijection on simplices, so $A,B$ are small quasicategories and $i$ remains degreewise injective. Reversing a join interchanges its two ordered blocks, so for every vertex $l$ there is a degreewise isomorphism
$$A\times_B B_{l/}\cong(K\times_L L_{/l})^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
It respects the projections: the final vertex $l$ becomes the initial vertex, and the initial variable face becomes the final variable face. Weak contractibility is unchanged by opposites. Explicitly, on the realization convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] the map $|T^{\mathrm{op}}|\to|T|$ sends $[x,(t_0,\ldots,t_n)]$ to $[x,(t_n,\ldots,t_0)]$. The formula for reversed operators makes this well defined under the quotient identifications, and the same formula is its continuous inverse. Thus every displayed strict outgoing comma for $i$ is weakly contractible.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.3.1, opposite join-comma identification; reversal calculation written explicitly.

proof.text: The strict pullback in Step 1 computes the infinity-categorical comma required by the comma criterion in Step 3. Indeed [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] gives the right fibration $L_{/l}\to L$. Opposites turn its right horn lifting problems into left horn lifting problems, since the missing index $r$ becomes $m-r$. Hence $B_{l/}\to B$ is a left fibration between quasicategories. By [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift] it is an isofibration. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] with $E=B_{l/}$, $T=A$ and $g=i$: the degreewise pullback $A\times_B B_{l/}$ is a quasicategory and represents $A\times_B^h B_{l/}$. Here $B_{l/}$ is a model of the coherent category of arrows out of $l$: [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence], applied to $\mathcal C=L$ and $y=l$, has $S_l=L_{/l}$ (since $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0=\Delta^{n+1}$ with the same operators) and gives an equivalence $\delta_l:L_{/l}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,L)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,L}\{l\}$ over $L$. Taking opposites, using $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,L)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$ with endpoints interchanged, gives an equivalence over $B$ from $B_{l/}$ to the arrow model $\{l\}\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$ used for $J_{j/}$ in the criterion. Cat$_\infty$ pullbacks of equivalent cospans agree, so $A\times_B B_{l/}$ is the comma $A\times^h_B B_{l/}$ of the criterion; all faces other than the fixed initial vertex remain variable. Thus the contractibility assumption of the cited comma criterion holds for exactly its infinity-categorical pullbacks, without treating an arbitrary strict pullback as a homotopy pullback.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.3.1, join-comma model; slice fibration and homotopy-pullback hypotheses checked.

proof.text: For each comma $T=A\times_B B_{l/}$, the map $T\to\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by Steps 1-2. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization] to this map, with Kan target $\Delta^0$. For every quasicategory $\mathscr C$, it identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,\mathscr C)$ with the full functor category on diagrams from $T$ inverting all edges, including all mapping spaces. Thus $T\to\Delta^0$ presents its localization at all edges. This verifies precisely the contractible-space-after-inverting-arrows convention in [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion]. Apply that criterion to $i:A\to B$: for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in a containing universe and every coherent diagram $H:B\to\mathcal E$, the actual restriction $\mathcal E_{H/}\to\mathcal E_{Hi/}$ is a functor equivalence over $\mathcal E$. This is its cocone-category conclusion, with no assumption that $H$ has a colimit.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Proposition 4.1.1.8, universal cocone conclusion.

proof.text: The map $i$ is degreewise injective between small quasicategories by Step 1, and Step 3 gives its universal cocone restriction property. The reverse implication in [lem-coef-universal-cocone-restriction-right-anodyne] therefore shows that $i=j^{\mathrm{op}}$ is right anodyne. This recognition lemma requires no full-subcategory hypothesis, as needed here.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.1.8 and Proposition 4.1.1.3(4), applied to the opposite monomorphism.

proof.text: Finally reverse the weakly saturated construction of $i$. Order reversal is an involutive automorphism of the category of simplicial sets, so it preserves pushout diagrams, ordinal-indexed colimit diagrams and arrow-retract equations. The opposite of the right horn inclusion $\Lambda_r^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $0<r\leq m$, is isomorphic to $\Lambda_{m-r}^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, with $0\leq m-r<m$. These are exactly the left horn generators in the statement. Thus the class of maps whose opposites are left anodyne contains all right horn generators and is closed under isomorphisms, pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. The minimality in [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne] implies that the opposite of every right-anodyne map is left anodyne. Apply this to $i$ and use $(j^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}=j$. At no point was the image assumed full.

source.place: Definition 2.0.0.3 and Proposition 4.1.1.3(4), explicit reversal of the weak saturation.
